findings.text: the disclosure says rewriting section 3's own paragraphs is "outside this node's write paths", but the node's dispatch fence lists docs/plans/serve-telemetry-spine.html as an exclusive write path and the node wrote to that file in this same commit (the appended landing record is part of the 17 added lines), so the reason recorded for leaving the stale prose in place is false; leaving it may be right -- the section prose is the spec and the followup owner should decide -- but as written the record tells a reader the node could not have amended it, and a reader comparing the two write-path lists (the fence's five paths against section 3's own three source files) cannot tell which one the sentence means.

the recorder's docstring states that "a probe that failed, is absent, or did not run this tick contributes no key at all", and ROW_SECTIONS at :90 repeats that "a present key always means a measurement" -- both of which the landed change excepts for the job table, whose every row now carries a marker-carrying jobs section on a tick where squeue did not answer; the file sits outside this node's fence so the drift is unowned, and it matters because the consumer's own contract denies the section the producer now emits, so a reader of serving_receipts.py would not expect it and may treat a marker as a measurement of the table.

the gate log begins with the pytest progress dots and names neither the revision, the tree, nor the command, so its "40 passed" cannot be tied to the content that produced it from the log alone; the two control logs in the same run do carry their mutation verbatim on line 1 and the sibling serve-provenance run writes "revision <sha> tree <path>" as its first line, so this is one log out of step with the wave's own convention rather than a missing convention, and the exposure is bounded: the manifest names 5c06b245 in its after_suite field.
